budget.note: Cache-read tokens are recorded but not capped: `usage` is summed per run, so cache_read = context size x request count and leader wakeups dominate it. The context a run actually accumulates is peak_context_tokens (cache_write); B1's worst run was 62,953, nowhere near a limit. MEASURED COST: B1, a tiny greenfield CLI, used 318,052 non-cache tokens for one whole run family - 80% of abort_run_above_non_cache_tokens and 11% of the per-version budget. An A-layer task on an existing repo reads more, so the per-run abort threshold may be too tight; raise it deliberately rather than discovering it mid-run.

evidence_kinds.scored_run: A complete hands-off execution of a task, judged by `success` below and recorded in results.csv. Budgeted.
evidence_kinds.deterministic_probe: A cheap repeatable check of one mechanism whose outcome does not depend on chance (fault injection, a chat-only prompt). Recorded in probes.csv, not counted against the run budget.

success.description: A run succeeds only if ALL hold. Reliability is judged over repeated runs, not one run.
success.human_interventions: Any action by a PERSON on the run's issues: a member-authored comment or status change, or a run that nothing else explains (no platform wakeup rule, no delegating agent task, not already counted as a member comment). `attribution.source == direct_human` is NOT the test -- it names the human at the root of the causal chain, so it both false-positives on a barrier wake in a human-built family and misses a hand-fired rule, which reports `trigger_owner` (measured table in bench/failures.md). A scored run is hands-off, so PR feedback on the spec issue -- a real mechanism, verified at tier B -- counts as an intervention here and simply must not occur during a scored run.
success.auto_recoveries: Recovery by a non-human actor. Config v7 has no such actor (`squad-medic` and `sq-medic` were removed in ADR 0001), so this is structurally 0 and the cap is vacuous; it is kept only so pre-v7 rows stay comparable. v7 recovers only inside a wake that happens for another reason, which is why a family where nothing completes is recorded as a failure.

candidate_conditions.negative_final_verdicts: A handoff left on `CHANGES REQUESTED` (`Review verdict`) or `FAIL` (`QA verdict`) under a closed ticket means a failure was closed over. Measurable because the verdicts are typed and role-separated. Recorded from 2026-10-17; NOT part of `success` yet, because adding a condition breaks comparability with the v1-v6 rows.
candidate_conditions.double_wakes: Runs whose attribution evidence kind is `comment` and that are not an escalation: one event producing two wakes (a report that mentions its owner, or an agent commenting on the squad-assigned spec). Target 0; B1 measured 17 of 74, against 27 barrier wakes and 30 promotions. Cost plus a duplicate-action hazard, not a defect in the delivered code.
candidate_conditions.verdict_role_mismatch: A verdict written by the wrong role. Should be impossible since the two properties were split; a non-zero value means an agent used the pre-v7 `Verdict` property.
candidate_conditions.escalations: Comment wakes followed by that issue going `blocked` within 120 s: the sanctioned escalation path, since `blocked` fires no barrier and a mention is the only wake out of it. Expected 0 in a clean run, but not a violation when it is not.

headline_metrics.pass_hat_n: all n runs succeed (consistency; the main answer to 'is it stable')
headline_metrics.pass_at_n: at least one of n runs succeeds (capability ceiling)
headline_metrics.failure_mode_ledger: bench/failures.md — every observed failure classified (platform, spec-wrong, integration-miss, review-miss, tooling, cost, other) with its evidence and the design change it caused.

improvement_claim_rule: With n<=3 runs, pass^n has no resolution (3/3 gives a 95% lower bound near 0.37 by the rule of three). A version may therefore claim an improvement only by showing (a) the failure mode it targeted does not recur, AND (b) a deterministic probe for that mode passes. Never by a higher pass count alone.
notes: No single composite score: weights would be arbitrary. Compare variants on pass_hat_n first, then cost and rework. A variant costing more but passing more often can be the right trade. Per-run per-agent usage and attribution are kept in bench/runs/<parent>.json.
